config.title: Flu Shot in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: When to get a flu shot in Berlin, measured against the city’s last four flu waves, who the STIKO recommends it for, who pays, and whether a pharmacy will do it.

items.q: When is the best time to get a flu shot in Berlin?
items.a: Aim for the last week of October or the first week of November. The RKI recommends October to mid-December, and the shot needs 10 to 14 days to work. Measured against Berlin’s four most recent ordinary flu seasons, a shot in the week of 2 November would have covered at least 95% of the lab-confirmed cases in every one of them, while a shot two weeks later already missed 14% of the early 2022/23 wave.

items.q: When does flu season peak in Berlin?
items.a: It moves. The Berlin peak week was 12 to 18 December in 2022, 5 to 11 February in 2024, 27 January to 2 February in 2025 and 19 to 25 January in 2026, based on RKI reporting data for lab-confirmed cases. Most winters peak between mid-January and early February, but the 2022/23 wave shows it can arrive before Christmas.

items.q: Is it too late to get a flu shot in December or January?
items.a: Not necessarily. The RKI says a flu shot can still make sense at the start of or during the flu wave, and in three of the last four Berlin winters the peak came in late January or February. You simply lose the part of the season that has already passed, so if you missed the autumn, take the first appointment you can get.

items.q: Who should get the flu vaccine in Germany?
items.a: The STIKO recommends it for everyone aged 60 and over, pregnant women from the second trimester or from the first with an underlying condition, people of any age with chronic conditions, residents of care homes, household contacts of people at risk, medical staff and staff in facilities with a lot of public contact, and people with occupational contact to poultry, wild birds, pigs or seals. For people 60 and over it recommends a high-dose or an adjuvanted vaccine.

items.q: Does health insurance pay for the flu shot if I am under 60?
items.a: If the STIKO recommends it for you, statutory health insurance pays. If you are under 60 with no medical or work reason, it depends on your fund. Many funds pay for all their members as an extra benefit, some only by reimbursement after you have paid, and some want a doctor’s recommendation. TK, for example, lists the flu shot for under-60s as a TK benefit. Ask your fund which route it uses before you book.

items.q: Can I get a flu shot at a pharmacy in Berlin?
items.a: Yes, if you are 18 or over. Trained pharmacists are allowed to vaccinate adults against flu, and many Berlin pharmacies run walk-in or booked slots in October and November. Bring your health insurance card. If the STIKO recommends the shot for you, the pharmacy bills your fund; if not, whether it is free depends on your fund’s arrangement with pharmacies.

items.q: How long does it take for the flu shot to work?
items.a: About 10 to 14 days. That is why the useful question is not when you get the shot but whether those two weeks end before the local wave starts. In Berlin the wave started to climb in late November in the early 2022/23 winter and between mid-December and early January in the other three.
